summary: Wasatch County, UT peak where a Uinta National Forest lookout station was maintained by 1914; the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the site as abandoned, and no source describes what remains.

facts.status_note: Listed by the Forest Fire Lookout Association as abandoned, not gone; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the top of the peak

access.note: Forest Service trailhead on the peak, reached by Forest Service roads and a one-mile trail from Wolf Creek Campground; no source describes lookout remains

visit.trail_note: Trailhead at the upper end of Forest Service Road 091; the one-mile Wolf Creek Peak Trail runs from Wolf Creek Campground

events.note: A January 1914 item calls the new Wolf Creek lookout station one where a lookout was maintained during dangerous fire seasons (Ogden Examiner, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Listed in the Association's table of Utah lookout sites and non-lookout structures with type Unknown and status Abandoned

evidence.supports: Wolf Creek Peak is within the Uinta National Forest
Wolf Creek Peak is in Wasatch County
the new Wolf Creek lookout station, maintained during dangerous fire seasons (January 10, 1914 Ogden Examiner item)
evidence.quote: the new Wolf Creek lookout station, one of the points on the Uinta forest on which a lookout is maintained during a dangerous fire season

evidence.supports: FFLA lists the site as Unknown type and Abandoned, among non-lookout structures
evidence.quote: Wolf Creek Peak Wasatch 40.47630 -111.02440 Unknown Abandoned

evidence.supports: trailhead on Wolf Creek Peak at the upper end of Forest Service Road 091
evidence.quote: The trailhead is located at the upper end of Forest Service Road 091 and lower end of Forest Service Road 050 on Wolf Creek Peak.

evidence.supports: one-mile Wolf Creek Peak Trail from Wolf Creek Campground to the upper trailhead
evidence.quote: The upper trailhead can be reached from Wolf Creek Campground via the one mile long Wolf Creek Peak Trail.

corrections.why: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the site as Abandoned, not gone, and no source found says the station structure was removed or what remains

notes_for_editor: The only history found is a 1914 item quoted secondhand on Forest Lookouts; the Ogden Examiner original was not read. No build date, design or end date was found. The brief's status 'gone' is not what the Association says ('Abandoned'), so it is proposed as unknown. The Forest Service page confirms a public trail to the peak but says nothing about lookout remains. Elevation and coordinates are not used. Worth checking Uinta NF archives or the Ogden Examiner for construction and closure dates. The Association's rule that sites move to the lookout lists applies to its Unknown/Undocumented Sites list, which does not include Wolf Creek Peak, so that rule is not used.
